name: Purpley Grey
lede: Purpley Grey is a soft, muted mauve-grey, one of two names the 2010 xkcd color survey built on top of [[medium-slate-blue]].

sections.title: A family-word compound
sections.body:
The survey treats "purpley" as a small word-family of its own, pairing it here with grey the way it paired [[pinky-purple]] with pink [1]. No book or earlier dictionary in our sources records the name; it is undocumented outside that 2010 survey [1]. Its ISCC-NBS fit is a pale reddish purple, 5.7 units off [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[vestal]], 3.1 units away and redder [2]. [[mountbatten-pink]] sits close behind, also redder, with [[dark-lavender]] nearly the same shade at 3.9 units [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this color in 35 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.15 percent, as photographed; a narrower, within-painting search finds it in 17 [3]. That puts it ahead of 63 percent of our named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, present in 8 of 1,674 paintings from that century, about 4.2 times the archive's typical rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, in 35 percent of its appearances, found by lightness rank rather than by eye [3].

Its most devoted painter is Claude Monet, who used it in 4 of the 50 of his works in the archive, 7.2 times his museums' baseline rate [3]. The earliest dated match is a work attributed to Sandro Botticelli from 1425, 585 years before the name's earliest record in 2010, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. That gap marks a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof the color or its name existed that early [3].
